component: ClientCore.run, step, confined, transaction; reused ForumCore.execute and render

claims.statement: Every accepted run has an AuthorizedTrace with actual step equations; every create requires Editor authority, and every edit also has an ownership/protected-cell guarantee.
Current and pending authority in accepted results remains owner-preserving and no stronger than initial supplied grants; Viewer never upgrades to Editor without an initial Editor source.
Successful core logout clears current and pending grants; the empty context cannot sign in without a new trusted offer. Failed HTTP batches roll back all actions.
For fixed program, context, public store and fuel, arbitrary private-vault changes leave publicView(run) equal; only Classified payload bodies are masked.
With all available authority confined to one observer and that observer's private value unchanged, arbitrary changes to other private values leave the complete Result equal.
Private values are readable only by their current authenticated owner, cannot become public post bodies and cannot drive conditions.
Every accepted trace Fits supplied fuel; each executed primitive or branch consumes one unit. No CPU/heap/parser bound is claimed.
Every accepted event originates from a matching operation or branch in the submitted syntax; input glyphs cannot introduce an operation.
Reused legal base transitions, ownership, text-only escaping and glyph/store size properties.
Rollback returns the original post store; Commit preserves the actual authorization trace; observer noninterference holds for the transaction output selected by the server.

assumptions: Correct Agda kernel and primitive definitions
Correct agda2hs, MAlonzo, GHC and runtime semantics for finite fully defined Haskell inputs
Trusted login offers, authentication, bearer-to-context binding, response routing and atomic commit integration
Correct glyph encoding and escaped HTML placement only in text nodes
Fixed-program, fixed-public-state observations; no timing or adaptive-client theorem
unverified: Byte, JSON nesting and AST node prechecks
Credential strength, token entropy, session storage/capacity, TLS, persistence
Browser parsing, response headers and rendering-to-browser semantics
CPU/heap/network/concurrency side channels and denial of service
Malicious code inside server process or authorized client copying plaintext outside the DSL
hashMeaning: SHA-256 binds bytes of sources, generated code, executable and evidence; it is not proof of translation correctness or authenticity.
